newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures fall after robust Q1 growth.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures fall after robust Q1 growth.

text.p: U.S. debt futures sliced some of Tuesday's steep gains, pressured by data showing robust first-quarter U.S. growth.
The Commerce Department said U.S. first-quarter gross domestic product rose 5.6 percent, the highest gain since 6.0 percent in the fourth quarter of 1987.
A Reuters poll of economists had showed a forecast for 4.1 percent, against 3.8 percent in the previous report.
June Treasury bond futures and nearby Eurodollars traded in a fast market after the GDP report, but activity has since tapered off, traders said.
The first-quarter price index rose 2.7 percent and the implicit price deflator gained 2.3 percent, both above expectations.
June T-bonds fell to 108-12/32 after the figures, but stabilized slightly above there.

"People might be a little bit long coming from yesterday, so there might be a sense of getting out here," one T-bond futures trader said. June T-bonds rallied 1-1/2 points on Tuesday on soft March durable goods and weaker-than-expected first-quarter labor costs. June T-bond open interest Tuesday rose 21,590 contracts, the exchange said.
The trader pegged support in June T-bonds at 108-2/32 to 108-12/32, with resistance at 108-21/32.
After Tuesday's open interest rise with good volume and higher prices, "the sense is you try to buy the dip a little bit," he said.
A Eurodollar trader noted aggressive volume after the GDP report, but said action had tapered off.
"If just really lacked followthrough," he said.
September euros were trading in the upper half of Tuesday's range, and off their morning lows.

Traders had scant reaction to New York purchasing managers data. The business conditions index fell to 50.9 in April versis 51.0 in March. The manufacturing index rose to 64.0 from 46.0 and non-manufacturing index fell to 49.4 from 51.6 in March.
Chicago purchasers data are due at 0900 CDT/1400 GMT. Chicago's April index was forecast at 56.2 from 57.5.

At 0840 CDT/1340 GMT, June T-bonds were down 10/32 to 108-20/32, 10-year notes fell 6/32 to 106-13/32, September Eurodollars were off 0.045 at 93.830 and December Eurodollars were 0.050 lower at 93.565.
